captions: 1:14 a.m. The only laundromat still open.
You type “you up?” Then you delete it.
412 names. Not one you can call right now.
The woman folding sheets doesn’t look up.
Then the drum stops. Silence. Just you.
And a whisper you forgot you knew: “Ya Allah.”
Fajr. 6:40 a.m. Snow on the street.
Footprints already. Someone walked to the mosque before you.
Inside, an old man smiles. “Salam, brother. Sit with us.”
You were never alone. Not for one minute.

post.caption:
412 contacts. 0 awake at 1:14 a.m. Allah never sleeps. 🤍

A laundromat at night. Machine 4, twenty-three minutes left. You type “you up?” and delete it. 412 names, and not one you can call. Then the drum stops, and in the silence a whisper you forgot you knew: “Ya Allah.”

“We are closer to him than [his] jugular vein.” (50:16)

Tonight, before you scroll: talk to Him first.
